about: Sources for the sentences added to the three side-project pages (voicelab, work-helper, barking-village) in round 9: in-browser demos and illustrations built on sample data, following Cesar's direction of November 11, 2026 (docs/case-study-answers.md, Q16–Q24). Same schema as docs/case-study-facts.json. Sentences that say something about a project come from the homepage (source homepage). Everything else describes how a demo works, defines a measure, or is sample data written for the page: source method, quoting the code or reference that backs it. No sentence here claims a feature, result, user, metric, stack or status beyond the homepage.

sources.method: How the demos on these pages work: web/projects/text-signals.js and web/projects/side-demos.js, the sample data written for them, and named methods (Flesch, 1948). Not a claim about any project.

facts.sentence: The library on the corner opens at nine. Most mornings, a short line forms outside before the doors unlock, and someone usually brings coffee for the staff. Inside, the reading room stays quiet until the school groups arrive. By noon the tables are full. People come to the library for the books, but many stay for the quiet, the long windows, and the sense that nobody is in a hurry.
facts.note: Original neutral sample paragraph written for the demo.

facts.sentence: It stays in this tab: nothing is sent or stored.
facts.note: True of the demo: side-demos.js makes no requests and uses no storage.

facts.section: Try the signals · Words per sentence
facts.sentence: Words per sentence 8 · 19 · 11 · 6 · 26
facts.note: Static fallback for the sample paragraph; tests/side-demos.test.js recomputes it.

facts.sentence: 14.0 words Words per sentence. It shows rhythm, not quality.
facts.note: Value is the sample paragraph's, recomputed by tests/side-demos.test.js.

facts.sentence: 0.76 53 of 70 words are distinct Distinct words divided by all words, the type/token ratio. It falls as a text gets longer, so compare texts of similar length.
facts.note: Value computed by text-signals.js on the sample paragraph (type/token ratio); recomputed in tests/side-demos.test.js.

facts.sentence: 11% seven letters or more A hint of density. It says nothing about whether a word is the right one.
facts.note: Value computed by text-signals.js on the sample paragraph (share of words with seven or more letters); recomputed in tests.

facts.sentence: 75 fairly easy Flesch reading ease: 206.835 − 1.015 × (words ÷ sentences) − 84.6 × (syllables ÷ words). Higher reads easier. Syllables are estimated, and the formula was made for English.
quote: Flesch, R. (1948). A new readability yardstick. Journal of Applied Psychology, 32(3), 221–233.
facts.note: Flesch reading ease computed by text-signals.js on the sample paragraph (Flesch 1948 formula); recomputed in tests.

facts.sentence: library ×2 quiet ×2 Most frequent words, leaving out common ones like “the” and “and”. Repetition can be a choice; this only counts it.
facts.note: Most repeated words computed by text-signals.js on the sample paragraph; recomputed in tests.

facts.sentence: None of these signals says who wrote a text.
quote: This experiment does not establish authorship.
